title: What development means

blocks.heading: What development means
blocks.text: Development is improvement in people's quality of life across economic, social, political and environmental dimensions. Economic development concerns productive opportunities and material resources. Social development concerns conditions such as health, education, shelter and adequate food. Political development concerns people's ability to participate, exercise rights and hold decision makers accountable. Environmental development includes improving living conditions while protecting the resources on which people depend.

blocks.heading: A project can have several effects
blocks.text: Consider an invented settlement where a new workshop offers paid jobs but releases dirty water into the stream used by households. More production and earnings are possible economic gains. Unsafe water is an environmental and social cost. Calling the project development merely because output rises overlooks those costs. A useful assessment asks who gains, who loses and whether the gains can last. If a treatment system removes the waste and can be maintained, jobs and cleaner water may be achieved together. If the workshop cannot afford to maintain that system, its installation alone does not settle the issue.

blocks.heading: Link the dimensions
blocks.text: This distinction underlies the rest of the subject. Production in Topic 3.1 explains how goods and services are created. Health in Topic 7.2 and education in Topic 7.3 show why services matter to people's lives. When considering any new activity, connect its economic effect to at least one effect on people or their environment. A higher money income is evidence about one dimension; it is not a complete description of development.
